core.cn: 核心意象：两张写着相反字样的卡片并排举起。

branches.en: The contrast branch: wet in the north, whereas dry in the south.
branches.cn: 对照分支：北方湿，而南方干。

branches.en: The legal branch: whereas the tenant has paid the rent.
branches.cn: 法律分支：鉴于承租人已付租金。

branches.en: The concession branch: whereas the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The register branch: whereas sounding formal next to while.
branches.cn: 语体分支：与 while 相比 whereas 更正式。

branches.en: The drafting branch: each recital opening with whereas.
branches.cn: 起草分支：每段陈述以 whereas 开头。

intro.en: Whereas is a fixed compound of where and as, and it no longer takes new endings; its closest relatives are whereby and whereon.
intro.cn: whereas 是 where 与 as 的固定复合词，不再接新词尾；最近的相关词是 whereby 与 whereon。

latinIntro.en: Latin marked the same contrast with autem and vero, and legal Latin used cum or quoniam for the reason clause; those are parallels, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 autem 与 vero 标记同样的对照，法律拉丁语用 cum 或 quoniam 引出理由从句；这些都是并行说法，不是祖源。

items.meaning: in what place, in which case
items.example: It is the first half of the word.
It marks the next event in a narrative.
items.exampleCN: 它标记叙述中的紧接事件。

items.meaning: although, and at the same time

items.example: It carries the contrast in whereas.
items.exampleCN: 它在 whereas 中承载对照。

definition_zh: 无论在哪里；在任何地方；四处
definition_en: in or to any place at all, or in every place that, used when the location does not need to be named
core_image: 一张没有边界的地图上，每个角落都插着一面小旗
scene: 她把地图铺开，随手在各个角落都插上小旗，说随便哪一面都行。Wherever you sit, you will hear the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 wherever 是「无论在哪里」（第 1 个义项：任何地点都可以）；句意为你坐在哪里，都能听见海声。地图每个角落都插着小旗，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 无论在哪里；凡是…的地方

senses.title: In any place at all
senses.titleCN: 无论在哪里；不管什么地方
senses.definition: used to say that every possible place is included
senses.definitionCN: 表示一切可能的地点都包括在内
senses.example: Wherever you sit, you will hear the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 你坐在哪里，都能听见海声。
senses.why: The suffix -ever turns where from a question into a total, exactly as it does for when and what.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ever 把 where 从问句变成全称，与处理 when、what 的方式完全相同。

senses.title: In every place that
senses.definition: used with a verb of scattered covering to mean in all the places concerned
senses.definitionCN: 与散布、覆盖类动词连用，指所涉及的每一处
senses.example: Wherever they went, the reporters followed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走到哪里，记者就跟到哪里。
senses.why: Covering all places means covering each place as it appears, so the word also marks repeated places.
senses.whyCN: 包揽所有地点也就是逐一覆盖每一处，于是这个词也标记重复出现的地点。

senses.title: Said alone, meaning any place suits
senses.definition: used as a short answer to say that no particular place is preferred
senses.definitionCN: 作简短回答，表示不偏好任何具体地点
senses.example: Wherever. The town is small and we can walk.
senses.exampleCN: 哪儿都行，小镇不大，走过去就好。
senses.why: One word takes the place of a whole list of possible sites, and so becomes an answer on its own.
senses.whyCN: 一个词替代一长串可能的地点，于是自成回答。

intro.en: Wherever is a Middle English compound of where and ever, made on the pattern of whatever and whichever.
intro.cn: wherever 是中古英语里 where 与 ever 的复合词，仿照 whatever、whichever 的模式构成。

items.en: Hwær and æfre were separate words, meaning where and ever.
items.cn: hwær 与 æfre 是两个分开的词，意为「何处」与「永远」。

items.en: The two were joined into wherever, which took over the older phrase in all places that.
items.cn: 两者连成 wherever，接管了旧说法「在所有的地方」。

items.en: The word spread through travel writing, where it marked any destination without naming it.
items.cn: 这个词在游记中传播，用来标记任何未点名的目的地。

items.en: Set phrases such as wherever possible made it common in official instructions.
items.cn: wherever possible 等固定短语让它在官方说明中变得常见。

items.en: In speech it also stands alone as a casual answer meaning any place is fine.
items.cn: 在口语中它还能单独作为随意回答，表示哪儿都行。

note.en: The first group gathers the -ever family and the opposite pairs, the second the words for any place and for everywhere.
note.cn: 第一组收 -ever 词族与成对的相反方向词，第二组收表示任何地方与到处说法。

entries.definition: The plain question word without the total sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不带全称意味的普通疑问词

entries.definition: The time version of the same compound.
A contrast word that shares the first half.
The heavy, old form of wherever.
In all places, stated rather than left open.
In any place, the plain phrase behind the compound.
In one unspecified place, narrower than wherever.

normalIntro.en: The word is where with ever on the end, so every point on the map is lit at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 where 加上结尾的 ever，于是地图上每一点同时亮起。

normal.en: Where stays in the question; wherever closes the question by covering all places.
normal.cn: where 留在问句里，wherever 用覆盖所有地点来关掉问句。

normal.en: The -ever trick works on every wh word: wherever, whenever, whoever, whatever.
normal.cn: -ever 这招对每个 wh 词都有效：wherever、whenever、whoever、whatever。

normal.en: Everywhere states the total; wherever leaves the door open.
normal.cn: everywhere 陈述全部，wherever 把门留着。

normal.en: Wherever possible is the commonest formal pairing.
normal.cn: wherever possible 是最常见的正式搭配。

normal.en: Said alone with a shrug, it means the place does not matter.
normal.cn: 耸着肩单独说出来，意思是地点无关紧要。

abstract.en: See flags planted in every corner of a map.
abstract.cn: 看地图每个角落都插上了旗。

abstract.en: Hear the same sea from every window.
abstract.cn: 从每一扇窗听到同一片海。

abstract.en: Feel a crowd follow someone from street to street.
abstract.cn: 感觉一群人从一条街跟到另一条街。

examples.en: Wherever she travels, she sends a postcard home.
examples.cn: 她无论去哪儿旅行，都会寄一张明信片回家。

examples.en: You can leave your bag wherever you like.
examples.cn: 你把包放哪儿都行。

examples.en: Wherever possible, the team works from home.
examples.cn: 只要有可能，团队就在家工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔艾佛」——威尔和艾佛说：人到哪儿，旗就插到哪儿。

root: 中古英语 where + ever 复合；同族有 wheresoever、whenever、whatever。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers every place, then spreads over each repeated place, and finally stands alone as a casual answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先包揽每一个地点，再铺到每一处重复出现的地方，最后单独站成随意的回答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small flags in every corner of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图每个角落都插着小旗。

branches.en: The open branch: wherever you sit, you hear the sea.
branches.cn: 开放分支：坐哪儿都能听见海。

branches.en: The spread branch: wherever they went, the reporters followed.
branches.cn: 分布分支：他们走到哪里记者就跟到哪里。

branches.en: The answer branch: wherever, the town is small.
branches.cn: 回答分支：哪儿都行，小镇不大。

branches.en: The formal branch: wherever possible in written rules.
branches.cn: 正式分支：书面规定中的 wherever possible。

branches.en: The family branch: wheresoever and whenever on the same plan.
branches.cn: 词族分支：wheresoever 与 whenever 同构。

intro.en: Wherever is where plus -ever, and the heavier -soever version still exists for legal and religious uses.
intro.cn: wherever 是 where 加 -ever，更重的 -soever 形式仍存在于法律与宗教文字中。

latinIntro.en: Latin used ubicumque for wherever, joining its place word with a generalising suffix; the entries below are the parallel forms, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ubicumque 表「无论何处」，把地点词与概括性词尾结合起来；下面条目是并行形式，不是祖源。

items.example: It is the first half of the word.
It states what wherever leaves open.
items.exampleCN: 它说出 wherever 留空的部分。

items.example: It is the plain phrase behind the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是复合词背后的白话短语。

items.example: It fixes the word in formal prose.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词固定在正式文字中。

definition_zh: 是否；不管…（还是…）；会不会（两件事中的哪一件）
definition_en: used to introduce two or more possibilities, especially a yes or a no, when the answer is not known
core_image: 岔路口立着一块牌子，一边写「是」一边写「否」
scene: 车停在岔路口，司机摇下车窗问路，路边只有一块牌子：一边是「是」，一边是「否」。I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 whether 是「是否」（第 1 个义项：引出知道与否尚未确定的一件事）；句意为我不知道他明天是否会来。岔路口一边「是」一边「否」的牌子就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 不管是出于偶然还是有意

senses.title: Yes or no
senses.definition: used to name two choices, usually whether something is so and whether it is not
senses.definitionCN: 引出两个选择，通常指某事成立与不成立
senses.example: I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道他明天是否会来。
senses.why: The word began as the Old English interrogative about two things, and the yes-or-no branch is the same fork seen without an answer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于古英语对两件事物的疑问，是与否两岔就是同一个岔口，只是没有答案。

senses.title: Either of two
senses.definition: used before two alternatives to say that neither one changes the result
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个并列选项前，表示两者都不改变结果
senses.example: Whether by accident or design, the paper arrived on the very last day.
senses.exampleCN: 不管是偶然还是有意，论文恰好在最后一天到了。
senses.why: When the two branches both lead to the same outcome, the fork stops being a question and becomes a condition.
senses.whyCN: 当两条岔路通向同一结果时，岔口不再问句，而成了一个条件。

senses.title: The question of if
senses.titleCN: 会不会；是否如此（作疑问的名词从句）
senses.definition: used after a verb of asking, knowing or doubting to introduce the matter in doubt
senses.definitionCN: 用在询问、知道、怀疑等动词之后，引出存疑的那件事
senses.example: They are still arguing about whether the plan is legal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仍在争论这个计划是否合法。
senses.why: A reported question loses its question mark, and whether is the word left holding the doubt.
senses.whyCN: 转述的问句丢掉了问号，whether 就成了那个承载疑问的词。

intro.en: Whether is the Old English pair hwæther or hwæder, which of two, and it has kept that fork-shaped meaning for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: whether 源自中古前的古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个），一千多年里一直保留这种分岔的意义。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked about a pair, unlike the plain what that asked about any thing.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 问的是一对中的哪一个，与询问任何事物的 what 不同。

items.en: Hwæther was the word for which of the two, and it could open a question or a clause.
items.cn: hwæther 是「两者中哪一个」的说法，既能开启问句，也能引出一个从句。

items.en: The final r weakened and was often dropped before a consonant, which gave the modern spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 词尾的 r 变弱，在辅音前常被吞掉，于是形成今天的拼写与读音。

items.en: The fixed pair whether or no (later whether or not) settled the alternative pattern in print.
items.cn: 固定的搭配 whether or no（后来作 whether or not）把这种两选句式固定在书面语里。

items.en: Grammar books sorted whether and if apart, keeping whether for careful writing and after prepositions.
items.cn: 语法书把 whether 与 if 分工，让 whether 留在严谨的文章和介词之后。

note.en: The first group collects the words that share the same wh shape, the second the words that also offer a choice or a condition.
note.cn: 第一组收与它字形相近的 wh 词，第二组收同样引出选择或条件的说法。

entries.definition: Not a question word at all, but the state of the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 天气（与 whether 读音几乎相同）

entries.definition: To dry up and shrink, one vowel apart.
The old word for to what place.
A different opening letter, meaning to a certain degree.
Can also mean whether, but never after a preposition.
One of the two, the older partner of whether.
Marks a doubt instead of naming the two branches.
Covers the either-or sense: it does not matter which.

normalIntro.en: Think of a road sign with two arrows, one saying yes and one saying no, and the word is the sign itself.
normalIntro.cn: 想一块画着两支箭头、一支写「是」一支写「否」的路牌，这个词就是那块牌子。

normal.en: Whether and weather sound the same, but one asks about a choice and one about the sky.
normal.cn: whether 与 weather 同音，但一个问选择，一个说天空。

normal.en: Whether or not: the or not is the second branch, made explicit.
normal.cn: whether or not：那个 or not 就是把第二条岔路说出来。

normal.en: After a preposition only whether works, as the decision was about whether to go.
normal.cn: 介词之后只能用 whether，例如决定是关于要不要去。

normal.en: The th in the middle links it to other and either, its old partner.
normal.cn: 中间那个 th 把它与 other、either 这些老伙伴连在一起。

normal.en: If two branches end in the same place, the question becomes a concession.
normal.cn: 若两条岔路通向同一处，疑问就变成让步。

abstract.en: See a fork in a road with no map.
abstract.cn: 想一个没有地图的岔路口。

abstract.en: Hear two arrows pointing opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 听两支箭头指向相反方向。

abstract.en: Feel the doubt of a question that expects no answer.
abstract.cn: 感受一个并不期待回答的疑问。

examples.en: Please tell me whether the shop is still open.
examples.cn: 请告诉我那家店是否还开着。

examples.en: Whether she likes it or not, the rules must be followed.
examples.cn: 不管她喜不喜欢，规则都必须遵守。

examples.en: The only question is whether we have enough time.
examples.cn: 唯一的问题是时间够不够。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂泽」——站在岔路口朝两边各喂一声：去还是不去？

root: 古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个）→ 中古英语 whether；同族有 either、other、whither。

sensesIntro.en: The word is born as a question about two things, turns into a neither-one-matters concession, and finally becomes the standard carrier of doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词生来就是对两个事物的疑问，转成「哪个都无所谓」的让步，最后成为承载疑问的标准说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost with a yes arrow and a no arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写着「是」与「否」两支箭头的路牌。

branches.en: The fork branch: he will come or he will not.
branches.cn: 岔路分支：他会来，或者不会来。

branches.en: The concession branch: whether by accident or design.
branches.cn: 让步分支：不管是偶然还是有意。

branches.en: The doubt branch: arguing about whether the plan is legal.
branches.cn: 存疑分支：争论计划是否合法。

branches.en: The grammar branch: whether after a preposition, never if.
branches.cn: 语法分支：介词之后用 whether，不用 if。

branches.en: The writing branch: careful prose keeps the full word.
branches.cn: 书面分支：严谨文章保留完整的词形。

intro.en: Whether is an old whole word, but its endings and its partners are transparent enough to take apart.
intro.cn: whether 是一个古老的整体词，不过它的词尾与搭档足够透明，可以拆开来看。

latinIntro.en: Latin marked a fork with utrum for the question and sive for the alternatives; the entries below are the borrowed counterparts, not ancestors of whether.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 utrum 表示疑问的分岔，用 sive 表示并列的选项；下面的条目是借入的对应词，并非 whether 的祖先。

items.example: It carries a fork in one word.
items.exampleCN: 它把岔口装在一个词里。

items.example: The same ending shows in other and either.
items.exampleCN: 同样的词尾出现在 other 和 either 中。

items.example: It answers the fork of whether.
items.exampleCN: 它回答了 whether 那个岔口。

items.example: It shares the ancient th ending.
items.exampleCN: 它共用了古老的 th 词尾。

items.example: It keeps the old wh question.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了古老的 wh 疑问。

items.example: It spells out the second branch.
items.exampleCN: 它把第二条岔路说出来。

items.example: It is the older and shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 这是更早也更短的形式。

items.example: It follows verbs such as decide.
items.exampleCN: 它跟在 decide 这类动词之后。

definition_zh: 哪一个；（关系代词）…的那个；（用于指前面整件事）这一点
definition_en: used to ask about one member of a known set, or to add information about a thing just named
core_image: 一排编号的抽屉，手指停在其中一个上面
scene: 抽屉柜前站着一排人，教练伸手在编号的抽屉上逐个点过，最后停在第三个上。Which of these bags is yours?
sceneCN: 这里 which 是「哪一个」（第 1 个义项：在已知的一组事物里问是哪一件）；句意为这些包里哪个是你的。手指在一排编号抽屉上逐个点过的动作就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: One out of a known set
senses.definition: used in a question to ask which member of a group or list is meant
senses.definitionCN: 在问句中询问某组或某份清单中的哪一个成员
senses.example: Which of these bags is yours?
senses.exampleCN: 这些包里哪个是你的？
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is to narrow a set down to one member, and that is still the core of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的任务就是把一组缩小成某一个成员，这至今仍是它的核心。

senses.title: The thing that
senses.definition: used after a noun to introduce a clause that identifies or describes that noun
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之后，引出对那个名词加以限定或描述的从句
senses.example: The book which she lent me is on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她借给我的那本书在桌上。
senses.why: A question about which member was reused as the link that points back to the member already chosen.
senses.whyCN: 询问哪一个成员的问句被借来作连接，指回已经被选定的那个成员。

senses.title: The whole fact
senses.definition: used with a comma to comment on the whole of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 与逗号连用，对刚说过的整件事发表评论
senses.example: He arrived two hours late, which annoyed everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟到两小时，这让大家都恼火。
senses.why: Once the clause can point back to a thing, it easily points back to an entire statement.
senses.whyCN: 从句一旦能指回一个事物，就很容易再指回整段陈述。

intro.en: Which is the Old English interrogative hwylc, a compound of hwa (who, what) and a suffix meaning like, so it began as what sort of.
intro.cn: which 是古英语疑问词 hwylc，由 hwa（谁、什么）与表示「像…那样」的词尾复合而成，本义是「什么样的」。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked about persons and things, and the compound added the idea of a kind.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 询问人与事物，复合之后又加上「种类」的意思。

items.en: Hwylc meant what kind of and was used to pick one thing out of a set.
items.cn: hwylc 意为「什么样的」，用来从一组中挑出一件。

items.en: The spelling settled as which, and the word took on the relative job alongside that.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 which，这个词除了 that 之外还承担了关系词的职能。

items.en: Writers began to split which for things and who for people, though the choice was still loose.
items.cn: 作者们开始让 which 指物、who 指人，尽管这种分工当时还不严格。

items.en: Modern usage lets which point back to a whole sentence, a use that who cannot take.
items.cn: 现代用法允许 which 指回整个句子，而 who 无法这样用。

note.en: The first group is the wh question family, the second the relatives that link a clause to a noun.
note.cn: 第一组是 wh 疑问词家族，第二组是连接从句与名词的关系词。

entries.definition: Asks with no list to choose from.
Same sound, no question at all.
The same family narrow to people.
Which, widened to any member.
The other common relative, more often for defining clauses.
The relative for people.
The object form, kept for formal prose.
Which plus a place, in the older grammar.

normalIntro.en: Which always works inside a set: point at the members first, then let the word choose one.
normalIntro.cn: which 总在一个集合里工作：先点出各个成员，再让这个词挑出一个。

normal.en: What opens the question; which opens the list.
normal.cn: what 打开问题，which 打开名单。

normal.en: The ch at the end is the same shape as a hand picking.
normal.cn: 词尾的 ch 像一只手在挑选。

normal.en: Add ever and no member can be left out: whichever.
normal.cn: 加上 ever，就没有成员能被排除：whichever。

normal.en: After a comma it can comment on the whole sentence.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，它可以评论整个句子。

normal.en: The which of a choice and the which of a relative are the same pointing finger.
normal.cn: 选择里的 which 和关系词里的 which 是同一根手指在指。

abstract.en: See numbered drawers and one finger moving along them.
abstract.cn: 想一排编号的抽屉和一根移动的手指。

abstract.en: Hear the short stop of a choice being made.
abstract.cn: 听做出选择时那一下短促的停顿。

abstract.en: Feel the narrowed field of a list instead of an open space.
abstract.cn: 感受名单收窄的场域，而不是一片空地。

examples.en: Which train goes to the airport?
examples.cn: 哪趟车去机场？

examples.en: This is the house which my grandfather built.
examples.cn: 这是我祖父盖的那座房子。

examples.en: She missed the last bus, which made her late.
examples.cn: 她错过了末班车，这让她迟到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威吃」——一堆包里只要吃的那一包，得先问：哪一个？

root: 古英语 hwylc（什么样的，由 hwa 与 -lic 复合）→ 中古英语 which；同族有 what、who、whichever。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts by narrowing a set to one member, turns that question into a relative link, and finally learns to point back at a whole statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先把一组缩小到某一位成员，再把那个问句变成关系连接，最后学会指回整段陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger moving along numbered drawers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着一排编号抽屉移动。

branches.en: The question branch: which of these bags is yours.
branches.cn: 问句分支：这些包里哪个是你的。

branches.en: The relative branch: the book which she lent me.
branches.cn: 关系分支：她借给我的那本书。

branches.en: The people branch: which for things, who for people.
branches.cn: 指人分支：which 指物，who 指人。

branches.en: The comment branch: which annoyed everyone.
branches.cn: 评论分支：这让大家都恼火。

branches.en: The derived branch: whichever covers every member.
branches.cn: 派生分支：whichever 覆盖每一个成员。

intro.en: Which is an old compound of the interrogative stem and a kind suffix, and it still takes ever and so as partners.
intro.cn: which 是疑问词干与「种类」词尾构成的古老复合词，今天仍以 ever、so 为搭档。

latinIntro.en: Latin used quis or qui for which, and the entries below are the borrowed roots rather than ancestors of which.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quis、qui 表示「哪个」，下面的条目是借入的词根，而非 which 的祖先。

items.example: It opens the whole wh family.
items.exampleCN: 它开启了整个 wh 家族。

items.example: It widens the choice to all.

items.exampleCN: 它加强 whichever 的语气。

items.example: It uses which as a link.
items.exampleCN: 它把 which 用作连接。

items.example: It shows which after a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 它显示 which 出现在介词之后。

items.example: It keeps the old kind suffix.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了古老的种类词尾。

definition_zh: 无论哪一个；随便哪一个；（从句）…的任何一项
definition_en: used to say that any one of a set will do, or to introduce a clause naming any member without saying which
core_image: 一整排门都被推开，随便进哪一扇都通向同一个院子
scene: 院子里一圈门全都敞着，无论走进哪一扇，最后都到同一个天井。Take whichever seat you like.
sceneCN: 这里 whichever 是「无论哪一个」（第 1 个义项：集合里随便哪一个都行）；句意为你想坐哪个座位都行。整排门全敞着、进哪扇都到同一个院子的画面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 无论哪一个；随便哪一个

senses.title: Any one will do
senses.definition: used to say that no member of a set is excluded and any choice is acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 表示集合中没有任何成员被排除，任何选择都可以
senses.example: Take whichever seat you like.
senses.exampleCN: 你想坐哪个座位都行。
senses.why: Adding ever to which removes the narrowing: every member of the set is now allowed.
senses.whyCN: 在 which 后面加 ever 就取消了收窄，集合里每个成员都被允许。

senses.title: No matter which
senses.titleCN: 无论哪一个（都不改变结果）
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause saying the result stays the same whichever member is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个从句，表示无论选哪一个，结果都不变
senses.example: Whichever road you take, the drive lasts an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 无论你走哪条路，车程都有一小时。
senses.why: The same total coverage also works as a concession, since the outcome does not depend on the pick.
senses.whyCN: 同样的全覆盖也能作让步，因为结果并不取决于挑哪一个。

senses.title: The one that turns up
senses.definition: used as a pronoun to mean any member of the set that fits the description
senses.definitionCN: 作代词使用，指集合中符合描述的任何一项
senses.example: Whichever of the two finishes first will report to me.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个谁先做完，就向我汇报。
senses.why: Because no member is fixed, the word must be able to stand as the subject of its own clause.
senses.whyCN: 因为没有固定成员，这个词就必须能充当自己从句的主语。

intro.en: Whichever is which plus the old emphatic ever, a combination that spread in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
intro.cn: whichever 是 which 加上古老的强调词 ever，这种组合在十五、十六世纪流行起来。

items.en: Hwylc was the simple word for which, with no widening at all.
items.cn: hwylc 只是单纯的「哪一个」，完全没有放宽。

items.en: The form ǣfre, meaning at any time, began to attach to question words.
items.cn: 意为「任何时候」的 ǣfre 开始黏附在疑问词上。

items.en: Whichever settled in print next to whatever and whoever, completing the set.
items.cn: whichever 与 whatever、whoever 一起固定进书面语，凑齐了这一组。

items.en: Grammar keeps whichever for a closed set and whatever for an open one.
items.cn: 语法上 whichever 用于封闭的集合，whatever 用于开放的范围。

items.en: In careful writing whichever is preferred for a choice among named things.
items.cn: 在严谨写作中，在已点明的事物之间做选择时更偏好 whichever。

note.en: The first group is the ever family, the second the words that also say it does not matter which.
note.cn: 第一组是 ever 家族，第二组是同样表示「哪个都无所谓」的说法。

entries.definition: The same word without the widening.
The ever form for an open set.
The ever form for people.
The same word plus way, a very common spoken pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 无论哪个方式（口语常用）

entries.definition: One or the other of just two.
One at random from an open group.
The person version of any one.
Whatever the route, a concession in three words.

normalIntro.en: Which asks the member; ever says the answer does not matter, so the two together cover the whole set.
normalIntro.cn: which 问成员是谁，ever 说答案无所谓，两者合起来就覆盖整个集合。

normal.en: Whichever works only inside a known list, so keep the list in view.
normal.cn: whichever 只在已知的名单里工作，所以要一直看着名单。

normal.en: Whichever for a closed set, whatever for an open one.
normal.cn: 封闭集合用 whichever，开放范围用 whatever。

normal.en: The stress falls on ev, and that stressed ever is the whole meaning.
normal.cn: 重音落在 ev 上，那个加重的 ever 就是全部意义。

normal.en: Swallowed whole, it often sounds like which-ever with a tiny pause.
normal.cn: 整块吞下去念，听起来像 which-ever，中间带一点停顿。

normal.en: Whichever comes first is the everyday English for this word.
normal.cn: whichever comes first 是这个词最日常的说法。

abstract.en: See every door standing open at once.
abstract.cn: 想所有门同时敞开。

abstract.en: Hear a shrug inside one word.
abstract.cn: 听一个词里藏着一次耸肩。

abstract.en: Feel the freedom of a choice that cannot go wrong.
abstract.cn: 感受一种怎样都不会错的选择自由。

examples.en: Choose whichever colour you prefer.
examples.cn: 你喜欢哪种颜色就选哪种。

examples.en: Whichever team wins, the final will be close.
examples.cn: 无论哪队赢，决赛都会很接近。

examples.en: Whichever of them calls first, tell me at once.
examples.cn: 他们谁先打来，立刻告诉我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为其饿」——为它饿着等：哪个先来就吃哪个，无论哪个都行。

root: which + ever（古英语 ǣfre，任何时候）→ whichever；同族有 whatever、whoever、whenever。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as which with the narrowing removed, becomes a concession when the result does not change, and finally stands alone as a pronoun.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词由取消收窄的 which 而来，在结果不变时成为让步，最后又能单独作代词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of doors all open on the same courtyard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排门全敞着，通向同一个院子。

branches.en: The permission branch: take whichever seat you like.
branches.cn: 许可分支：想坐哪个座位都行。

branches.en: The concession branch: whichever road you take.
branches.cn: 让步分支：无论走哪条路。

branches.en: The subject branch: whichever finishes first reports to me.
branches.cn: 主语分支：谁先做完就向我汇报。

branches.en: The closed-set branch: only among known things.
branches.cn: 封闭集合分支：只在已知事物之间。

branches.en: The stress branch: the ever carries the accent.
branches.cn: 重音分支：ever 部分承载重音。

intro.en: Whichever is easy to take apart: the question word plus the old free-standing ever.
intro.cn: whichever 很好拆：疑问词加上古老而可独立使用的 ever。

latinIntro.en: Latin formed the same idea with quicumque, one word that already contains the total sense; the entries below are counterparts, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quicumque 一个词就表达了同样的全覆盖之意；下面的条目是对应形式，并非来源。

items.example: It makes a concession in three words.
It is the everyday spoken pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这是最日常的口语模式。

latinEntries.meaning: whichever of the two you please

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而；（一段时间）一会儿
definition_en: during the time that something happens, and also used to contrast two facts or to name a short period of time
core_image: 两条平行的钟表指针同时走着，一条走完另一条还在动
scene: 厨房里水在烧，她一边等一边切菜，两个动作同时进行。She read the paper while the water was boiling.
sceneCN: 这里 while 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：在某事进行的那段时间里）；句意为水开的时候她在看报纸。两条平行走的指针同时指着的画面就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used to say that one thing happens during the same period as another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一件事与另一件事发生在同一段时间内
senses.example: She read the paper while the water was boiling.
senses.exampleCN: 水开的时候她在看报纸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a stretch of time, and a clause placed inside that stretch gives the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思只是一段时间，把从句放进这段时间里就产生了「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit a fact that makes the main point surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用在从句开头，承认一个使主句令人意外的事实
senses.example: While the plan is cheap, it will take years to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划虽然便宜，却要花好几年才能完成。
senses.why: Two things placed side by side invite comparison, and when the second weakens the first the word leans to although.
senses.whyCN: 两件事并排摆放就会引来比较，当第二件削弱第一件时，这个词便偏向 although。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个事实，显示二者不同
senses.example: Some people talk a lot, while others say nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人话很多，而另一些人什么都不说。
senses.why: The same side-by-side picture becomes a plain contrast when the two facts are simply weighed against each other.
senses.whyCN: 同样是并排的画面，当两个事实只是彼此对照时，就成了单纯的对比。

senses.title: A period of time
senses.definition: a short period of time, usually after the words a or for
senses.definitionCN: 一小段时间，通常跟在 a 或 for 之后
senses.example: Wait here for a while and I will be back.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里等一会儿，我就回来。
senses.why: This is the noun behind the conjunction: a while is the stretch of time that the clause later filled in.
senses.whyCN: 这是连词背后的名词：a while 就是后来被从句填进去的那段时间。

senses.title: To pass time pleasantly
senses.definition: in while away, to spend time in a relaxed way until it has passed
senses.definitionCN: 在 while away 中，指轻松地度过一段时间
senses.example: We whiled away the afternoon on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩上打发了整个下午。
senses.why: If a while is a block of time, then while away is the act of letting that block be used up.
senses.whyCN: 如果 a while 是一块时间，那么 while away 就是让那块时间被用掉的动作。

intro.en: While began as the Old English noun hwīl, a period of time, and only later became the conjunction that fills such a period.
intro.cn: while 起初是古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间），后来才成为填充这段时间的连词。

items.en: The stem hwī- meant a rest or a span of time in the older Germanic languages.
items.cn: 在较早的日耳曼语中，词干 hwī- 指一段休息或一段时间。

items.en: Hwīl was a noun, and the phrase þā hwīle þe, the time that, was its full form.
items.cn: hwīl 是名词，完整形式是 þā hwīle þe，意思是「…的那段时间」。

items.en: The long phrase shrank to while that and then to plain while, which took over the conjunction job.
items.cn: 长短语缩短为 while that，再缩成 while，连词职能便由它承担。

items.en: While spread into contrast and concession, replacing older words in ordinary prose.
items.cn: while 扩展到对比与让步，在普通文章中取代了更早的说法。

items.en: The noun survives in a while, once in a while and while away, keeping the original time sense.
items.cn: 名词义保存在 a while、once in a while 与 while away 中，保留了最初的时间意味。

note.en: The first group is the words one letter away in shape, the second the time and contrast words that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是字形只差一点的词，第二组是承担同样职能的时间与转折词。

entries.definition: A very large sea animal, one letter longer.
The same word with a t, common in British prose.
A trick, and the same shape as the verb in while away.
A high complaining sound.
The preposition version of the same time relation.
Two things happening at the same moment.
The full concession word behind sense two.
The formal contrast partner of while.

normalIntro.en: Hold two films running side by side, and while is the word that ties their frames together.
normalIntro.cn: 想两部并排播放的影片，while 就是把两边的画面绑在一起的那个词。

normal.en: A while is a block of time, so the conjunction simply puts a clause inside the block.
normal.cn: a while 是一块时间，连词就是把从句放进这块时间里。

normal.en: Side by side can mean at the same time, in contrast, or in spite of.
normal.cn: 并排既可以是同时，也可以是对比，还可以是让步。

normal.en: While away means letting the block of time run out pleasantly.
normal.cn: while away 是让那块时间愉快地流走。

normal.en: British writing adds a t and says whilst; ordinary speech does not.
normal.cn: 英式书面语加个 t 说 whilst，日常口语则不这样用。

normal.en: After a comma, while begins the second of two weighed facts.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，while 引出两个被比较事实中的第二个。

abstract.en: See two clock hands turning at the same pace.
abstract.cn: 想两根同时同速转动的钟表指针。

abstract.en: Hear water boiling under a quiet page turning.
abstract.cn: 听水开的声响下面是翻书声。

abstract.en: Feel a stretch of time with nothing urgent in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一段没有急事的时光。

examples.en: He called while I was cooking dinner.
examples.cn: 我做晚饭的时候他打来了电话。

examples.en: While I agree with you, I cannot support this plan.
examples.cn: 虽然我同意你的看法，却无法支持这个计划。

examples.en: Let us rest for a while before we continue.
examples.cn: 我们歇一会儿再继续吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外欧」——望外一瞧，时间悄悄流过去一会儿。

root: 古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间）→ 中古英语 while；同族有 whilst、meanwhile、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a block of time, then fills that block with a clause, then weighs two clauses, and finally keeps the plain noun in a while and while away.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一块时间开始，用从句把这块时间填满，再让两个从句相互权衡，最后把朴素的名词义留在 a while 与 while away 里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two clock hands moving side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根并排走动的钟表指针。

branches.en: The simultaneity branch: boiling water and a newspaper.
branches.cn: 同时分支：烧水与看报。

branches.en: The concession branch: while the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The contrast branch: some talk, while others say nothing.
branches.cn: 对比分支：有人话多，有人沉默。

branches.en: The noun branch: wait for a while.
branches.cn: 名词分支：等一会儿。

branches.en: The phrasal branch: whiling away an afternoon.
branches.cn: 短语分支：打发一个下午。

intro.en: While is a free Old English word; its family is made by compounds such as meanwhile and by the old -st form whilst.
intro.cn: while 是古英语的自由词；它的词族由 meanwhile 这类复合词和古老的 -st 形式 whilst 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin covered the same ground with dum and interim; the entries below are parallel forms, not the source of while.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 dum 与 interim 表达同样的意思；下面的条目是平行形式，并非 while 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作连词。

items.example: It keeps the old noun alive.
items.exampleCN: 它让古老的名词义活下来。

items.example: It repeats the noun in idiom.
items.exampleCN: 它在习语中重复这个名词。

items.example: It turns time into a verb.
It is the bridge to the conjunction.

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而（英式书面，同 while）
definition_en: a British and rather formal form of while, used to say that two things happen at the same time or that two facts differ
core_image: 同一个钟面上多加了一个小小的 t 形刻度
scene: 一封英式公函里写道：请在此等候，同时我们核对手续。Please wait whilst we check your documents.
sceneCN: 这里 whilst 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：与 while 同义的英式书面形式）；句意为请在此稍候，我们核对一下您的证件。同一个钟面上多出一个 t 形小刻度的画面就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used in formal British writing to say that one thing happens during the time of another
senses.definitionCN: 在正式英式写作中表示一件事发生在另一件事进行的那段时间里
senses.example: Please wait whilst we check your documents.
senses.exampleCN: 请在此稍候，我们核对一下您的证件。
senses.why: Whilest arose as an adverbial form of while, and the extra ending never changed the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: whilest 本是 while 的副词形式，多出的词尾从未改变「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used in formal writing to admit a fact that makes the main clause surprising
senses.definitionCN: 在正式写作中承认一个使主句显得意外的事实
senses.example: Whilst the results are encouraging, more tests are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，还需要更多测试。
senses.why: Because the word is only a formal twin of while, it inherits every sense of its partner.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是 while 的正式孪生形式，所以继承了搭档的全部义项。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used in formal prose to set two facts against each other
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文章中把两个事实并排对照
senses.example: Some departments grew, whilst others were cut.
senses.exampleCN: 有些部门扩大了，而另一些被裁减。
senses.why: A formal register suits official documents, where contrasts are stated plainly and without emotion.
senses.whyCN: 正式语体适合公文，那里对比总是平铺直叙、不带情绪。

senses.title: A marker of style
senses.definition: used to give a formal or slightly old-fashioned tone to a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 为文章添上正式或略带古旧的语气
senses.example: The notice reads: no entry whilst the lights are on.
senses.exampleCN: 告示上写着：灯亮时禁止入内。
senses.why: The t survives mainly because of print and legal habits, not because it says anything extra.
senses.whyCN: 这个 t 主要靠印刷与法律习惯保留下来，并不因为它多表达了什么。

intro.en: Whilst is while with the old adverbial ending -st, the same one that produced amongst and against.
intro.cn: whilst 是 while 加上古老的副词词尾 -st，与 amongst、against 的一模一样。

items.en: The noun hwīl meant a period of time; there was no form ending in -st yet.
items.cn: 名词 hwīl 意为一段时间，当时还没有以 -st 结尾的形式。

items.en: A new shortening whilest appeared beside while, built with the old ending -es or -st.
items.cn: 与 while 并列出现了一个缩短的形式 whilest，由古老的词尾 -es 或 -st 构成。

items.en: Printers settled the spelling whilst, and it spread in British official prose.
items.cn: 印刷商把拼写定为 whilst，它在英式公文中传播开来。

items.en: American usage dropped whilst almost entirely and kept while.
items.cn: 美式用法几乎完全舍弃了 whilst，只保留 while。

items.en: British writers keep it as a marker of formal or slightly elderly style.
items.cn: 英国作者保留它，作为正式或略带回旧语体的标志。

note.en: The first group collects the other -st forms that look alike, the second the plain words whilst can always be replaced by.
note.cn: 第一组收其他形近的 -st 形式，第二组收随时可以替换 whilst 的朴素说法。

entries.definition: An old form of the plural, easily mistaken for whilst.
entries.definitionCN: while 的旧复数形式，易与 whilst 混淆

entries.definition: Among with the same old ending.
An old -st form that became the standard one.
Drop the final t and the word becomes the everyday one.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉词尾 t 就是日常的 while

entries.definition: The everyday twin, used in all registers.
Two things at one moment, shorter and plainer.
The clear concession word for formal prose.
During the whole of a period, not just part of it.

normalIntro.en: Take while and hang the old ending -st on it, and you have the formal British twin.
normalIntro.cn: 把 while 拿出来挂上古老的词尾 -st，就得到了英式正式的孪生词。

normal.en: Whilst is never a different meaning, only a different tone.
normal.cn: whilst 从来不是另一个意思，只是另一种语气。

normal.en: Amongst, against and whilst share the same old -st.
normal.cn: amongst、against 与 whilst 共用一个古老的 -st。

normal.en: If in doubt, write while; whilst belongs to letters and notices.
normal.cn: 拿不准就用 while，whilst 属于书信与通告。

normal.en: American editors strike out the t almost always.
normal.cn: 美国编辑几乎总会把这个 t 划掉。

normal.en: The l before st is heard in careful speech and lost in fast speech.
normal.cn: st 前的 l 在慢读时听得见，快读时则消失。

abstract.en: See a formal seal pressed onto an everyday word.
abstract.cn: 想一枚印章盖在日常词上。

abstract.en: Hear a clerk saying it aloud in an office.
abstract.cn: 听一位办事员在办公室里念出它。

abstract.en: Feel the small weight of an unnecessary letter.
abstract.cn: 感受一个多余字母带来的分量。

examples.en: Please wait whilst we check your documents.
examples.cn: 请在此稍候，我们核对一下您的证件。

examples.en: Whilst the results are encouraging, more tests are needed.
examples.cn: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，还需要更多测试。

examples.en: He kept his coat on whilst the room was cold.
examples.cn: 屋里冷的时候他一直穿着外套。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪欧斯特」——在正式场合歪着身子等一会儿，多带了个 t 就更客气。

root: 中古英语 whilest（while 加古词尾 -st）→ 现代英语 whilst；同族有 while、amongst、against。

sensesIntro.en: The word is only the formal twin of while: the same during, concession and contrast senses, wearing the old -st ending as a style marker.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词只是 while 的正式孪生：同样的同时、让步与对比义项，只是戴着古老 -st 词尾作为语体标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock face with one extra tick mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟面上多出一个小刻度。

branches.en: The simultaneity branch: waiting whilst documents are checked.
branches.cn: 同时分支：核对证件时等待。

branches.en: The concession branch: whilst results are good, tests continue.
branches.cn: 让步分支：结果虽好，仍要测试。

branches.en: The contrast branch: some grew whilst others were cut.
branches.cn: 对比分支：有人扩大，有人被裁。

branches.en: The register branch: notices and formal letters.
branches.cn: 语体分支：通告与正式书信。

branches.en: The regional branch: kept in Britain, dropped in America.
branches.cn: 地域分支：英国保留，美国舍弃。

intro.en: The only thing to analyse here is the old ending -st, which also shaped amongst and against.
intro.cn: 这里唯一要分析的是古老的词尾 -st，它同样塑造了 amongst 和 against。

latinIntro.en: The ending is native Germanic, so no Latin source stands behind it; the entries below are parallel conjunctions.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词尾是本土地日耳曼成分，背后没有拉丁来源；下面的条目是平行的连词。

items.example: It kept the ending for good.
It replaces whilst before a noun.

definition_zh: 鞭子；抽打；（快速）搅打（奶油、蛋）；(议会)党鞭
definition_en: a long thin strip of leather on a handle, used to strike animals, and the quick beating motion made with it
core_image: 一条皮鞭在空中甩出一个急速的弧线
scene: 马厩前，骑手抬手一甩，皮鞭在空气里划出弧形的响声，马立刻加快脚步。The driver cracked the whip and the horses ran faster.
sceneCN: 这里 whip 是「鞭子」（第 1 个义项：带柄的长皮条，用来抽打牲畜）；句意为车夫甩响鞭子，马跑得更快了。皮鞭在空中甩出急速弧线的画面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 抽打；快速搅打；猛地移动

senses.title: The leather tool
senses.definition: a long thin strip of leather or cord fixed to a handle, used for striking
senses.definitionCN: 固定在柄上的细长皮带或绳索，用来抽打
senses.example: The driver cracked the whip and the horses ran faster.
senses.exampleCN: 车夫甩响鞭子，马跑得更快了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the object itself, which was first a quick-moving instrument for driving animals.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是这件物体本身，起初是一种快速挥动、用来驱使牲畜的工具。

senses.title: To strike with it
senses.definition: to hit a person or animal with a whip, or as if with one
senses.definitionCN: 用鞭子或仿佛用鞭子击打人或动物
senses.example: The rain whipped against the windows all night.
senses.exampleCN: 雨整夜抽打着窗户。
senses.why: The verb came straight from the noun, and from hitting it widened to anything that hits sharply and fast.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接由名词而来，从击打又扩展到任何迅猛而尖锐的拍打。

senses.title: To beat food quickly
senses.definition: to beat cream, eggs or a mixture quickly with a fork or whisk until air is folded in
senses.definitionCN: 用叉子或打蛋器快速搅打奶油、蛋或混合物，使空气混入
senses.example: Whip the cream until it holds soft peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 把奶油搅打至能形成柔软的尖角。
senses.why: The fast circular motion of a whip in the air is the same motion as a whisk in a bowl.
senses.whyCN: 鞭子在空中甩出的快速绕圈动作，与打蛋器在碗里的动作完全相同。

senses.title: To move suddenly
senses.definition: to move or take something out suddenly and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 突然而迅速地移动或抽出某物
senses.example: She whipped out her phone and took a photo.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地掏出手机拍了一张。
senses.why: The curve of a cracking whip is a picture of pure speed, so the verb took on the meaning to move in that shape.
senses.whyCN: 甩响的鞭子那一道弧线就是纯粹的速度，于是动词也带上了那样移动的意思。

senses.title: The party official
senses.definition: in a parliament, the member whose job is to keep the party together and see that members vote
senses.definitionCN: 在议会中负责维持本党团结、督促议员投票的成员
senses.example: The chief whip warned the party not to split.
senses.exampleCN: 党鞭长警告党内不要分裂。
senses.why: A hunting term for the rider who keeps the hounds together was borrowed for the official who rounds up votes.
senses.whyCN: 一个狩猎术语指把猎犬聚拢起来的骑手，后来借指把选票聚集起来的官员。

intro.en: Whip comes from Middle English wippen, to swing or snatch quickly, and the noun for the tool followed.
intro.cn: whip 源自中古英语 wippen（快速挥动或抓取），表示工具的义项随之出现。

items.en: The family of fast-moving words included the ancestors of whip and of wippen in other Germanic tongues.
items.cn: 这个表示快速动作的词族包含 whip 在其他日耳曼语言中的祖先形式。

items.en: Wippen meant to move nimbly or to snatch, and the noun wippe named the swinging tool.
items.cn: wippen 意为轻快移动或抓取，名词 wippe 指挥动的工具。

items.en: The verb covered beating, whipping and the fast beating of cream, and hunting gave the word its pack sense.
items.cn: 动词涵盖抽打、鞭打与快速搅打奶油，狩猎语境又给了它「成群领袖」的意思。

items.en: Industry made whiplash and whip-round part of everyday speech, and the adjective whippy followed.
items.cn: 工业与日常生活让 whiplash、whip-round 成为常用语，形容词 whippy 也随之出现。

items.en: Parliamentary usage fixed the political whip in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 议会用法在十九世纪把政治意义上的 whip 固定下来。

note.en: The first group is the look-alike words that differ by one sound, the second the words that also mean to hit or to beat food.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个音的近形词，第二组是同样表示击打或搅打的说法。

entries.definition: A thin twisting strand, as of smoke or straw.
The hand that holds the whip, and so the advantage.
To clean with a cloth, one vowel apart.
A small piece broken off; a different opening sound.
To strike with the end of a whip, and the cord itself.
The general verb for stirring or hitting hard.
The kitchen tool for whipping, and to move it fast.
To beat someone severely as a punishment.

normalIntro.en: Every sense of whip comes from one picture: a thin strip travelling very fast through the air.
normalIntro.cn: whip 的每个义项都出自同一幅画面：一条细长的皮条极快地穿破空气。

normal.en: The wh of the crack is in the word: whip sounds like the strike.
normal.cn: 甩鞭的响声就在词里：whip 听起来就像那一下抽打。

normal.en: Air, horse, cream, phone: the same fast curve in four places.
normal.cn: 空气、马背、奶油、手机：同一个快速弧线用在四处。

normal.en: To whip up a meal is to make it in the time of one crack.
normal.cn: whip up 一顿饭就是用一下响鞭的时间做出来。

normal.en: The party whip rounds up votes the way a huntsman rounds up hounds.
normal.cn: 党鞭聚拢选票，就像猎手聚拢猎犬。

normal.en: Double the p before -ed and -ing: whipped, whipping.
normal.cn: 在 -ed 和 -ing 前要双写 p：whipped、whipping。

abstract.en: Hear a sharp crack and then the beat of hooves.
abstract.cn: 听一声脆响和随后急促的马蹄声。

abstract.en: See a thin line bending in the air.
abstract.cn: 想一条细线在空气中弯折。

abstract.en: Feel the sting that arrives a moment later.
abstract.cn: 感受稍后才到的火辣辣的痛。

examples.en: He keeps a long leather whip on the wall.
examples.cn: 他墙上挂着一根长皮鞭。

examples.en: Whip the eggs with a little sugar.
examples.cn: 把鸡蛋加少许糖搅打一下。

examples.en: The wind whipped the flags above the gate.
examples.cn: 风把门上的旗子抽得猎猎作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威扑」——威风一扑，皮鞭抽出一条弧线。

root: 中古英语 wippen（快速挥动、抓取）→ whip；同族有 whiplash、whipping、whip-round。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a fast-moving tool, becomes the act of striking with it, then the fast beating of food, then any sudden movement, and finally the official who keeps a party in line.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一件快速挥动的工具开始，变成用它的击打，再变成快速搅打食物，再变成任何迅猛的动作，最后指维持本党一致的官员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leather strip drawn fast through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条皮条急速抽过空气。

branches.en: The object branch: the driver cracks the whip.
branches.cn: 物体分支：车夫甩响鞭子。

branches.en: The strike branch: rain whipping the windows.
branches.cn: 击打分支：雨抽打窗户。

branches.en: The kitchen branch: whipping cream to soft peaks.
branches.cn: 厨房分支：把奶油打至软尖。

branches.en: The speed branch: whipping out a phone.
branches.cn: 速度分支：猛地掏出手机。

branches.en: The political branch: the chief whip warns the party.
branches.cn: 政治分支：党鞭长警告全党。

intro.en: Whip is a whole Germanic word, and it grows by compounding and by phrases rather than by prefixes.
intro.cn: whip 是一个完整的日耳曼词，它靠复合与短语生长，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used flagellum for the tool and verbera for the blows; the entries below are borrowed counterparts, not ancestors of whip.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 flagellum 指鞭子，用 verbera 指鞭打；下面的条目是借入的对应词，并非 whip 的祖先。

items.example: The same word is tool and action.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词既是工具也是动作。

items.example: It also means to stir up feeling.
It turns the sound into a metaphor.
It refers to the rein hand.

definition_zh: 低声说；耳语；悄悄说；沙沙作响
definition_en: to speak very quietly, using breath rather than voice, so that only a person close by can hear
core_image: 一个人凑到另一个人耳边，用手挡着嘴，只放出一点气声
scene: 图书馆里，有人俯身凑到同伴耳边，用手挡着嘴，只放出一点气声。She leaned over and whispered the answer in my ear.
sceneCN: 这里 whisper 是「低声说、耳语」（第 1 个义项：只用气声而不振动声带地说话）；句意为她探过身来，在我耳边小声说出答案。凑到耳边、用手挡嘴、只放出一点气声的动作就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To speak with breath
senses.definition: to say something in a very quiet voice, without vibration of the vocal cords
senses.definitionCN: 用极轻的声音说话，声带不振动
senses.example: She leaned over and whispered the answer in my ear.
senses.exampleCN: 她探过身来，在我耳边小声说出答案。
senses.why: The word imitates the sound itself: a hissing movement of breath without voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词摹拟的就是声音本身：一股只有气、没有嗓音的嘶嘶气流。

senses.title: To sound softly
senses.titleCN: 沙沙作响；发出轻柔的响声
senses.definition: to make a soft continuous sound like a quiet stream or moving leaves
senses.definitionCN: 发出像细流或树叶摇动那样的轻柔连续声响
senses.example: The leaves whispered as the wind moved through them.
senses.exampleCN: 风穿过树叶，树叶沙沙作响。
senses.why: Anything that sounds like breath without a voice can be said to whisper, so the word moved from people to nature.
senses.whyCN: 凡听起来像无嗓音气息的东西都能说是在低语，于是这个词从人扩展到了自然。

senses.title: To talk in secrets
senses.definition: used of people passing information quietly, often news that is not yet public
senses.definitionCN: 指人们悄悄地传递消息，常常是尚未公开的新闻
senses.example: People whisper that the company is about to be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 人们私下议论说这家公司即将被出售。
senses.why: Quiet words travel only between close ears, so telling a secret and whispering became the same act.
senses.whyCN: 轻细的话只在近处的耳朵之间传递，于是说秘密和低语成了同一个动作。

senses.title: The quiet sound itself
senses.definition: as a noun, the quiet sound of speech without voice or of a soft rustle
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指不带嗓音的轻声话语，或轻微的沙沙声
senses.example: They spoke in a whisper so the baby would not wake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们低声说话，免得吵醒孩子。
senses.why: The noun simply turns the act into a thing, and it also names the sound of a stream.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是把动作变成事物，同时也用来称溪流的声音。

intro.en: Whisper is a Middle English word of imitative origin, first written whispren, and its form has hardly changed since.
intro.cn: whisper 是中古英语的摹声词，最早写作 whispren，此后词形几乎没有变化。

items.en: Old English had hwisprian for murmuring, built from a base that already imitated a hiss.
items.cn: 古英语已有 hwisprian（喃喃低语），其词根本身就摹拟嘶嘶声。

items.en: The verb appeared as whispren and whisperen, and the noun followed close behind.
items.cn: 动词写作 whispren、whisperen，名词紧随其后出现。

items.en: The word gained its secret-telling sense, and to whisper news came to mean to spread a rumour.
items.cn: 这个词获得了「悄悄传话」的意思，whisper news 便指散布传言。

items.en: Nature writers used it for the sound of leaves and streams, widening the picture.
items.cn: 自然文学作家用它形容树叶与溪流的声音，扩大了这幅画面。

items.en: The noun stays in fixed phrases such as in a whisper and a whisper of doubt.
items.cn: 名词义保留在 in a whisper 与 a whisper of doubt 这类固定短语里。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same quiet shape, the second the ways of speaking at low volume.
note.cn: 第一组收字形相近的同族安静词，第二组收低声说话的各种说法。

entries.definition: A thin curl of smoke or hair.
The shrill sound made through the lips.
A stiff hair on an animal's face.
The quiet sound taken as a noun.
A low continuous sound with voice in it.
To speak unclearly, with mouth nearly shut.
The sharp breath sound of s.
The soft sound of leaves or paper moving.

normalIntro.en: The word is built out of the sound it names: a hiss of air with no voice behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是用它所命名的声音拼出来的：一股没有嗓音的气流嘶嘶作响。

normal.en: Say it very quietly and the word performs itself.
normal.cn: 轻声把这个词念出来，它就在演示自己。

normal.en: The whis at the start is the same hiss as in whistle.
normal.cn: 开头的 whis 与 whistle 里的嘶声相同。

normal.en: No voice, only air: that is the difference from speaking quietly.
normal.cn: 只有气没有嗓音：这就是它与小声说话的区别。

normal.en: Leaves, streams and rumours all whisper.
normal.cn: 树叶、溪流和传言都会 whisper。

normal.en: In a whisper keeps the noun, while whisper to keeps the verb.
normal.cn: in a whisper 留住名词义，whisper to 留住动词义。

abstract.en: Feel warm breath at the edge of an ear.
abstract.cn: 感受耳畔一股温热的气。

abstract.en: See a hand cupped beside a mouth.
abstract.cn: 想一只手挡在嘴边。

abstract.en: Hear a room where nobody raises a voice.
abstract.cn: 听一个谁都不提高嗓子的房间。

examples.en: Do not whisper in class; ask me after the lesson.
examples.cn: 上课别小声说话，下课来问我。

examples.en: He whispered a few words and she nodded.
examples.cn: 他小声说了几句，她点了点头。

examples.en: A whisper ran through the crowd before the result was read.
examples.cn: 结果宣读之前，人群里传开了一阵低语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威斯珀」——威斯珀凑到耳边只吹气不出声。

root: 古英语 hwisprian（喃喃低语，摹声词）→ 中古英语 whisperen → 现代英语 whisper。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as voice-less breath, then lends that sound to leaves and streams, then to secrets passed between close ears, and finally stands as a noun for the soft sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从无嗓音的气流开始，把这声音借给树叶与溪流，再借给近耳之间传递的秘密，最后作为名词指那轻柔的声音本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath released beside an ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：在耳边放出的一口气。

branches.en: The quiet speech branch: the answer whispered in my ear.
branches.cn: 轻声说话分支：在我耳边说出的答案。

branches.en: The nature branch: leaves whispering in the wind.
branches.cn: 自然分支：风中的树叶沙沙作响。

branches.en: The rumour branch: people whisper that the firm will be sold.
branches.cn: 传言分支：人们私下议论公司将被出售。

branches.en: The noun branch: speaking in a whisper.
branches.cn: 名词分支：低声说话。

branches.en: The idiom branch: a whisper of doubt.
branches.cn: 习语分支：一丝疑虑的低语。

intro.en: Whisper is an imitative whole word; its family is built with -ing, -er and -y rather than with real prefixes.
intro.cn: whisper 是摹声的整体词，它的词族靠 -ing、-er、-y 构成，而不是靠真正的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used susurrus for a whisper, itself an imitation of the sound; the entries below are counterparts, not ancestors of whisper.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 susurrus 表示低语，它本身也是摹声词；下面的条目是对应形式，并非 whisper 的祖先。

items.example: The hiss is in the letters.
It joins the word to politics.
items.exampleCN: 它把此词与政治连起来。
